patients.summary: High school math teacher with recurrent UTIs and familial severe hypertriglyceridemia on fenofibrate, joined in 2024. Pyelonephritis in February 2025, pyelonephritis again at 30 weeks of pregnancy, delivered in November, then hypertriglyceridemia-induced necrotizing pancreatitis with infected necrosis and septic shock four weeks postpartum. Recovered by spring 2026, back on fenofibrate.

conditions.label: Recurrent urinary tract infection
conditions.note: several cystitis episodes a year at prior practice

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

orders.order: Request records from prior primary care office

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient. 27 yo F, teaches math at a high school, moving her care here before the school year starts. Prior PCP was in the next county; records requested today.

Two standing issues:

1. Triglycerides. Told in her early twenties that her triglycerides were very high, has been on fenofibrate 145 mg every day since. Takes it reliably. Never had pancreatitis. Her dad has the same problem, and his father had pancreatitis. Doesn't drink at all. Tries to keep fat and sugar down but admits the school lunchroom doesn't help.

2. UTIs. Has had bladder infections on and off since her early twenties, several a year at the worst stretch. Each one treated with a few days of antibiotic from her old office. Never on daily prophylaxis, never seen urology. None since the spring.

No surgeries. NKDA. Mother has type 2 diabetes. Never smoked, no alcohol, no drugs. Married. Exercise: walks most evenings.

ROS: no abdominal pain, no dysuria now, no fevers, no weight change, mood good.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Well-appearing. HEENT unremarkable, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly, no CVA tenderness. Skin: no xanthomas. Ext no edema.

PHQ-9 2.

Assessment / plan
- Hypertriglyceridemia, severe by history, on fenofibrate. Continue 145 mg daily. Fasting lipids today along with CMP. Talked about keeping simple sugars and fat low.
- Recurrent UTI: currently well. Call early with symptoms so we can treat promptly.
- Health maintenance: CBC, TSH, A1c (mom with DM2), one-time HIV and hep C screening today. Pap 2023 per her report, will confirm from records. Flu shot in the fall.

Return in about 4 months for a lipid recheck.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Jasmine,

Your labs are back. Kidney, liver, blood count, thyroid and A1c all look fine. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative.

Triglycerides came back at 410 with an HDL of 34. That's high but well below the range where pancreatitis becomes a real worry, so fenofibrate is doing a lot of the work. Because triglycerides are over 400, the lab can't calculate an LDL, which is normal for the report.

Keep the fenofibrate going and we'll recheck in December.

Best,
your primary care physician

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records received by fax, 19 pages, from the patient's previous primary care office. Scanned to media.

Summary for the chart (MA abstraction):
- Problem list: hypertriglyceridemia on fenofibrate 145 mg daily; recurrent cystitis, treated episode by episode with short antibiotic courses, several per year.
- Pap smear 2023: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- HPV vaccine series completed as a teenager.
- Allergies: none listed.

Abstracted by MA. Forwarded to PCP for review.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In after school for vaccines. No fever today, no prior reactions. Influenza vaccine to L deltoid and 2024-25 COVID vaccine to R deltoid, VIS given for both. Waited 15 minutes without problems. Lot numbers in the immunization record.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for the lipid recheck we planned in August. Taking fenofibrate daily, no muscle aches, no abdominal pain. Holiday season at school means a lot of baked goods in the faculty room, she says, and she's been trying to steer clear. No urinary symptoms since joining.

O: Vitals reviewed. Comfortable. Abdomen soft, nontender. No xanthomas.

A/P: Hypertriglyceridemia on fenofibrate. Fasting lipids and CMP today; expect them in the same range as summer. Same dose. Asked her to let us know before trying to conceive, since we will need to plan around the fenofibrate. Recheck in about six months.

documents.title: Lipid results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Jasmine, triglycerides 438 this time, about where they were in August. Liver and kidney tests fine. No change for now; same fenofibrate. Enjoy the break when it comes.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic refill request from patient's pharmacy for fenofibrate 145 mg, #90. Last filled October. Last lipid visit 12/10. Sent per protocol, 90 days with one refill.

documents.title: After-hours call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Patient texted then called. Burning and frequency started late last week, then fevers and shaking chills, and now an ache in the right flank that is getting worse. Has been trying to push through it with fluids. Not pregnant as far as she knows. Can keep fluids down.

Sounds like pyelonephritis with several days of fever. Advised she go to the emergency department tonight rather than wait for a morning visit. She agreed; will go to the regional hospital ED. Asked her to message us when she knows the plan.

events.reason: Fever, chills and right flank pain

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily to complete 10 days of antibiotics

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD (received by fax 2/10/2025)
Arrival 02/04/2025 01:40

CC: fever, chills, R flank pain x 5 days

HPI: 28 yo F, hx recurrent UTIs and hypertriglyceridemia, with five days of fever and rigors and right-sided flank pain along with dysuria and urinary frequency. No nausea, vomiting or diarrhea. Sent in by her PCP.

Meds: fenofibrate 145 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA. PMH: recurrent UTI, hypertriglyceridemia. No surgeries. Never smoker, no EtOH.

VS: T 38.9 C (102.0 F), HR 110, BP 130/85.
Exam: febrile, uncomfortable. Right CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft. 

Labs: WBC 15.0, Hgb 13.2, Plt 250. UA with pyuria, LE positive, nitrite positive. Urine hCG negative. Blood cultures x2 drawn, no growth to date. Urine culture sent, pending.

Impression: acute pyelonephritis with fever and tachycardia.
Plan: IV ceftriaxone started. Admit to medicine.

Addendum (inpatient team, discharge 02/08/2025): fever and right flank pain persisted through 72 hours of ceftriaxone; renal ultrasound without hydronephrosis or collection. Afebrile from day 4. Discharged on ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID to complete 10 days. PCP follow-up within one week.

documents.title: Hospital follow-up scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: ED record from the regional hospital received by fax this morning and routed to PCP. Called patient, home since Saturday. Scheduled hospital follow-up Wed 2/12 at 4:00.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after her admission for right pyelonephritis, 2/4 to 2/8. The ED record came over Monday; the rest is from her.

She says the fevers kept going for the first three days on IV antibiotic and the flank pain didn't budge, so they did a kidney ultrasound, which she was told was normal. Turned the corner on day 4. Home Saturday on ciprofloxacin, two days left. No fever since discharge. Flank is just a little sore if she presses on it. Eating normally. Back at school yesterday.

She never heard what grew in the urine culture. We have no culture report either; called the hospital lab, not available to us by phone. She is improving on cipro regardless.

Exam: afebrile, vitals in flowsheet. Looks well. Minimal R CVA tenderness, abdomen soft and nontender.

A/P
- Acute pyelonephritis, resolving. Finish ciprofloxacin. CBC, BMP and UA today. Call for any fever or return of flank pain.
- Hypertriglyceridemia: on fenofibrate. Lipids due again in early summer.
- Recurrent UTI background noted.

documents.title: Labs from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your white count is back to normal and kidney function is normal. Urine looks clean now. Nice recovery. Finish the last cipro doses today and tomorrow.

documents.title: Positive test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning! I took a test this morning and it's positive. My last period started Feb 27. We're really happy. What do I do about the fenofibrate? I took it last night.

documents.title: RE: Positive test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Congratulations, Jasmine! By your dates you're about 5 weeks.

Please stop the fenofibrate now; we don't use it in pregnancy. One dose last night is nothing to worry about. I've updated your medication list.

I've put in a referral to obstetrics so they can get your first prenatal visit on the calendar. Reach out any time.

documents.title: Refill request declined
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy auto-refill request for fenofibrate 145 mg. Medication was stopped 4/3 (pregnancy). Declined and pharmacy asked to inactivate the auto-refill. Called pt to let her know; she has been seeing the OB group since late April.

documents.title: Records for OB
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my OB's office asked for my immunization history and my last labs. Can you send them over? Their fax number is on the form I'm uploading.

documents.title: RE: Records for OB
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Jasmine, we faxed your immunization record, your August and December 2024 labs and the February hospital follow-up note to the OB office this morning. Confirmation received.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. About 24 1/2 weeks pregnant by her LMP, prenatal care with the outside OB group, who tell her everything is on track. Feeling well. Summer off; back in the classroom in two weeks.

No urinary symptoms since February. Off fenofibrate since April. No abdominal pain.

Meds: none from us. NKDA.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Gravid abdomen, nontender. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No CVA tenderness. Ext: no edema.

PHQ-9 3.

A/P
- Pregnancy, followed by OB.
- Recurrent UTI: no episodes since February; call promptly with any symptoms.
- Hypertriglyceridemia: off fenofibrate for the pregnancy.
- Health maintenance: Pap due next year. Flu shot when it comes in; fine during pregnancy.

Follow up after delivery.

events.reason: Fever and right flank pain at 30 weeks

conditions.label: Infections of kidney in pregnancy, third trimester

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth four times daily to complete 14 days of antibiotics

documents.title: Obstetric Triage Note
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC TRIAGE NOTE (received 10/01/2025)
Date of service 09/25/2025

28 yo G1 at 30w0d by LMP, followed by our group. Two days of fever and chills with constant right flank pain that radiates into the lower abdomen. Nauseated, no vomiting. Pyelonephritis earlier this year (February). Recurrent UTIs. Hypertriglyceridemia, on fenofibrate per home list. NKDA.

T 38.6 C (101.5 F), BP 120/78, HR 110. FHR 160.
Right CVA tenderness. Uterus soft, nontender.
UA: pyuria, bacteriuria, hematuria. CBC with leukocytosis and left shift.

A: acute pyelonephritis in pregnancy, 30 weeks.
P: admit to antepartum, IV ceftriaxone, continuous monitoring initially. Discharged 9/27 afebrile on cephalexin 500 mg QID to finish 14 days. Follow up in OB clinic next week.

documents.title: Kidney infection again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just a heads up that I was admitted Thursday night through Saturday with another kidney infection, right side again. Fever, the whole thing. Baby was fine the whole time. They gave me IV antibiotics and sent me home on cephalexin 4x a day for the rest of two weeks. Feeling much better. Do I need to come in?

documents.title: RE: Kidney infection again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, and I'm glad you and the baby are OK. You don't need to come in this week if you're improving. Our nurse will call you Thursday to check on you, and I'll ask the OB office to send their note. Get your flu shot with us next week and we'll recheck your urine then.

documents.title: Nurse follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Follow-up call after antepartum admission for pyelonephritis. Pt reports no fever since Saturday, flank pain gone, taking cephalexin four times a day with no GI upset. Good fetal movement. OB follow-up done yesterday. Confirmed nurse visit Tuesday for flu vaccine and UA. OB triage note received yesterday and filed.

conditions.label: Infections of kidney in pregnancy, third trimester

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 31 weeks. Finished cephalexin yesterday. Afebrile, no urinary symptoms, no flank pain. Clean-catch UA collected; dipstick negative for leukocytes, nitrite and blood, PCP reviewed. Influenza vaccine (2025-26 trivalent) given L deltoid, VIS reviewed, no prior reactions. Tolerated well.
